candidates.title: SWSC: Compressing Large Language Models via Sharing Weights for Similar Channels
candidates.venue: International Conference on Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence
candidates.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have spurred development in multiple industries. However, the growing number of their parameters brings substantial storage and computing burdens, making it essential to explore model compression techniques for parameter reduction and easier deployment. We propose an LLM compression method based on the concept of “Sharing Weights for Similar Channels” (SWSC). It uses the K-Means clustering algorithm to cluster model weights by channel, generating clusters with highly similar vectors within each. A codebook vector from each cluster is selected to approximately replace all vectors in the cluster, significantly reducing the number of model weight parameters. On the other hand, we approximate the error weight matrix generated by compression using low-rank matrices, aiming to compensate for the LLM performance loss caused by a small number of outliers during the approximation process. Experimental results show that SWSC can effectively maintain the performance of compressed LLMs even under low-precision conditions. Furthermore, our method can be used orthogonally with mainstream compression techniques to further reduce the resource consumption of LLMs.
candidates.reason: チャネル単位で重みベクトルをクラスタリングし、類似チャネルの重みをコードブックベクトルで共有して置き換え、低ランク近似で圧縮誤差を補うSWSCを提案する。LLMのパラメータ数と保存・計算負担を減らす圧縮機構であり、推論展開への直接貢献が確認できる。

candidates.title: SHOQ: Stability-Aware Hierarchical Quantization by Identifying Critical Outliers for LLMs
candidates.venue: International Conference on Communication, Computing & Security
candidates.abstract: The deployment of Large Language Models (LLMs) is severely constrained by their massive parameter scale, making quantization a critical enabling technology. However, the prevalence of outlier weights significantly limits the efficacy of traditional quantization methods. Existing research typically treats these outliers as a uniform group, overlooking the variability in their importance stability across different contexts. This oversight leads to coarse protection strategies, hindering the optimal balance between compression efficiency and model accuracy. This paper proposes a novel framework for stability-aware outlier handling and hierarchical quantization. First, we design a stability identification method combining multi-strategy data sampling with Bayesian optimization. By introducing an “in-channel relative contribution” metric, we precisely evaluate the frequency with which outlier weights are identified as important, thereby isolating key outliers with high stability. Subsequently, we propose a hierarchical quantization algorithm that implements three-level differentiated bit-width allocation (FP16/INT8/INT4) based on the stability-frequency mapping of outliers, while applying activation-magnitude-based group quantization (INT4) to non-outlier weights. Experimental results on mainstream LLMs (LLaMA series) demonstrate that our method significantly reduces perplexity (PPL) and improves zero-shot task accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods (GPTQ, AWQ, SpQR) at the same bit-width. This provides an effective pathway for the high-accuracy, high-efficiency deployment of LLMs.
candidates.reason: LLM量子化で外れ値の重要度の安定性が文脈で変わる点に着目し、多戦略サンプリングとベイズ最適化で安定性を同定して階層的に量子化するSHOQを提案する。重み外れ値の保護を一律から安定性依存へ変える量子化機構であり、推論向け圧縮への直接貢献が確認できる。

candidates.title: Clairvoyant: Predictive Shortest-Job-First Admission for Serial LLM Inference
candidates.abstract: Serial LLM inference backends process requests sequentially under First-Come-First-Served (FCFS) admission, causing Head-of-Line Blocking (HOLB) under mixed workloads: short factual queries can be delayed by minutes behind long generation jobs. While cloud-scale deployments mitigate HOLB via continuous batching (e.g., vLLM, Orca), these solutions require tens of gigabytes of VRAM for concurrent KV-caches, rendering them infeasible for memory-constrained edge and local deployments that rely on serial request dispatch. We present Clairvoyant, a drop-in sidecar proxy for serial OpenAI-compatible backends (e.g., Ollama, llama.cpp) that implements predictive Shortest-Job-First (SJF) admission. Clairvoyant predicts response length using 19 lightweight lexical features via an ONNX-exported XGBoost classifier, achieving 0.029 ms per-request latency. Because admission scheduling relies on relative ranking rather than exact token prediction, Clairvoyant captures over 95% of the ranking fidelity of fine-tuned transformers at a fraction of the computational cost. We also uncover a critical dataset bias: curated instruction datasets are degenerate training sources for length prediction, as GPT-imposed brevity constraints reduce Long-class representation to under 0.02% of examples, establishing natural conversation logs as the only viable training signal. End-to-end evaluations demonstrate substantial latency reductions across diverse hardware regimes: a 70-76% short-request P50 latency reduction on an RTX 4090, a 69.7% reduction on Apple M1 edge hardware, and an 83.6% reduction in Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) on a GCP NVIDIA L4 real-world trace replay (rho = 0.80). Clairvoyant is open-source, requires zero modifications to the inference backend, and provides a low-overhead mechanism to eliminate HOLB in edge LLM environments.

candidates.title: QuantaSpike: Short-Window Spike-Driven Quantization for Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) achieve strong performance across many tasks but rely on dense multiply-accumulate (MAC) operations during inference, resulting in high energy cost. Spiking neural networks (SNNs) offer an event-driven alternative in which synaptic integration uses lightweight accumulation. However, spike-driven LLM inference remains difficult because outlier-heavy activations typically require long firing windows or auxiliary non-spiking paths. We propose QuantaSpike, a short-window spike-driven quantization framework for LLMs built around Logarithmic Ternary Integrate-and-Fire (LTIF) neurons. LTIF uses ternary events with power-of-two membrane-response quanta, improving the information represented by each firing step while retaining shift-ACC-compatible computation. QuantaSpike combines this neuron with group-adaptive gain and selective outlier admission: normal values use residual LTIF steps, whereas admitted outliers receive one additional onset spike before entering the same residual dynamics. Across OPT and Llama-2, QuantaSpike achieves state-of-the-art or competitive perplexity and zero-shot accuracy among spike-driven LLM quantization methods. It also transfers to newer dense LLMs, remaining close to the FP16 reference on Llama-3-8B and Qwen3-8B under the same four-step firing window. Analytical linear-energy projections show that QuantaSpike reduces the energy of one linear transformation by about $80.0\%$ on OPT models and $67.1\%$ on Llama-2 models relative to SpikeQuant, providing an accurate and energy-efficient spike-driven path for LLM inference.
candidates.reason: LLM推論のエネルギー費用を下げるため、対数三値の発火型ニューロンと群適応ゲイン、外れ値の選択的許容を組み合わせた短窓スパイク駆動量子化QuantaSpikeを提案する。推論時の乗算累積を軽い累積へ置き換える量子化機構で、直接貢献が確認できる。

candidates.title: ChainFlow: Few-Step Latent Flow Matching for Speculative Decoding
candidates.abstract: Speculative decoding has become a standard way to accelerate LLM inference: a lightweight drafter proposes tokens that the target verifies in one parallel pass. Existing drafters face trade-offs that limits their speedups: autoregressive drafters generate tokens one at a time, so drafting cost grows with draft length, while diffusion drafters generate tokens in parallel but predict each position independently, ignoring inter-token dependencies. We introduce ChainFlow, a new speculative decoding paradigm and the first flow-matching drafter conditioned on the target's hidden states. ChainFlow treats drafting as a short transport over hidden states, needing one or two flow steps instead of the many denoising steps of generation from noise. A variational autoencoder compresses these states so drafting cost barely grows with target size, lightweight feedback heads restore inter-token dependencies, and tree drafting raises acceptance. On Qwen3.5 models, at matched drafter size and training data, ChainFlow outperforms EAGLE-3 and DFlash in vLLM by 39% and 11%, respectively. These gains further widen as drafters are adapted to new languages sequentially. Our ablations cover drafter design and concurrent serving, and we open-source our code and drafter models.
